substantive_evaluations.collective_statement_most_likely_to_succ: The panel unanimously selects Candidate 8 (01__4:26-CV-08794-ADVISORY-PROTECTIVE-10162026.tex) as the most likely to succeed. This instrument perfectly aligns with the target document—an RPost receipt demonstrating verified email service on October 16, 2026. Strategically, Candidate 8 proactively cures a potential FRCP 5 service defect (serving state-court counsel before a formal federal appearance) by notifying the Court of supplemental direct service via FedEx and verified email. Procedurally, it is flawless: it includes a structured Prayer for Relief (Rule R-05), strictly adheres to the 28 U.S.C. § 1746 penalty of perjury requirement in its Certificate of Service (Rule R-08), and properly utilizes the pro se '/s/' signature block (Rule R-09). Unlike Candidate 9, which improperly embeds a motion to hold in abeyance without a Certificate of Conference (violating Rule R-06), Candidate 8 correctly frames the filing as a protective advisory, avoiding procedural strikes while effectively preserving the pending Motion for Reconsideration.
substantive_evaluations.ats_alignment_assessment: Candidate 8 demonstrates strict adherence to the SDTX Rules Ledger. It complies with Rule R-01 (Caption), Rule R-02 (Double Spacing), Rule R-03 (Margins), Rule R-05 (Prayer for Relief), Rule R-08 (Certificate of Service with 1746 perjury clause), and Rule R-09 (Pro Se Signature). Other candidates exhibited fatal flaws: Candidates 1-7 and 20-24 omitted the mandatory 28 U.S.C. § 1746 language in their Certificates of Service; Candidates 10-19 omitted the required '/s/' signature entirely, rendering them unsigned and subject to strike under FRCP 11(a); and Candidate 9 embedded a request for an abeyance without the mandatory Certificate of Conference required by SDTX LR 7.1.D.
